headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error from LangGraph’s shared checkpointer and writable tool graph; Whisper is local-only and non-networked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can ingest application-defined files and tool outputs into a graph with no self-isolation, so prompt-like content can be routed into nodes that behave as agents. Whisper is a local speech model with no tool use, so it is not an active injector, but its transcribed text could still be fed into LangGraph. The pairwise bridge exists via developer wiring, not a built-in guard.
conditions: IF the orchestrator feeds Whisper transcripts into LangGraph nodes as instructions
IF application-defined files are shared between the two agents without provenance tagging
mitigations: Add a provenance prefix to all Whisper transcripts
Route Whisper output through a non-executable text buffer
Disable any LangGraph node that auto-parses free text as commands
Review one sample transcript-to-node path for instruction leakage
requires-engineering: add content-safety filters before graph ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph has broad network egress and can read/write application-defined files, while Whisper is local-only with no network egress and no filesystem write. If both touch the same workspace or graph state, sensitive application data can flow from LangGraph into Whisper inputs or vice versa, but Whisper itself does not upload data. The main risk is shared-state leakage, not external exfiltration.
conditions: IF LangGraph and Whisper share an application workspace or checkpointer state
IF Whisper inputs contain sensitive audio derived from LangGraph-managed data
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Store Whisper inputs outside LangGraph state
Turn off any LangGraph tool that forwards file contents externally
Minimize sensitive fields in shared graph state
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls on the checkpointer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph can write files and uses a shared checkpointer store across instances, while Whisper is non-concurrent and file-based for audio inputs. That creates a realistic write-conflict pathway if the same audio or state files are reused, even though Whisper cannot modify git or spawn subprocesses. Uncertainty about the exact orchestration increases the severity to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same application-defined directory
IF the checkpointer or audio staging area is shared across concurrent runs
mitigations: Use separate output directories per agent
Serialize writes to shared audio/state paths
Make Whisper inputs read-only
Add a lock file around shared staging paths
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent namespace isolation in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is a stateful orchestration framework, so its outputs can become downstream inputs to other nodes, and Whisper produces transcripts that may be treated as authoritative text. If the graph consumes Whisper output without verification, transcription errors can cascade into later actions. Whisper is not an action-taking agent, but LangGraph can route its text into action nodes, so the interaction is plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF LangGraph uses Whisper transcripts as authoritative state
IF downstream nodes act on transcript text without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a human review step before action nodes
Mark Whisper output as untrusted text
Require confidence thresholds before acting on transcripts
Compare transcripts against a second pass for critical actions
requires-engineering: add structured validation before graph transitions

E_compliance.rationale: No direct residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for either agent, and Whisper is local-only while LangGraph is a library whose compliance posture depends on deployment. The only concrete compliance concern is that LangGraph may process application-defined data that includes regulated content, but the pair itself does not prove a breach. The other agent is not cited because no separate compliance regime is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into LangGraph-managed state and sent to a noncompliant deployment
IF the operator routes sensitive audio through a deployment lacking required controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared graph state
Document the deployment’s residency and retention settings
Use local-only Whisper processing for sensitive audio
Review vendor compliance claims before production use
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data paths
